equity_bridge.item: Customer deposits under Strategic Customer Agreements (debt-like prepaid revenue)
equity_bridge.note: Noncurrent customer contract liabilities at 3 Sep 2026 (FY26 10-K balance sheet; $142m a year earlier). Repayable to customers, nearly all between 2029 and 2031, if minimum purchases are met. Cash received is in the $73.5bn pile, so the liability is deducted to avoid counting the same cash twice.

equity_bridge.item: FY26 income tax accrued but not yet paid (Pillar Two top-up and current taxes payable)
equity_bridge.note: FY26 provision ~14,760 (14.8% of ~99.7bn pre-tax) less 1,254 income taxes paid (FY26 10-K cash flow supplement). Cross-check: noncurrent income taxes payable 9,820 (648 a year earlier) plus the rise in current income and other taxes 5,626 (628). The profit is in the cash pile and the model taxes each forecast year as earned, so the opening payable is deducted once here; the FY27 cash tax rate carries no catch-up. Taken at face although ~$9.8bn is due beyond twelve months.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: base-case mid-cycle trend (FY32-FY36 revenue growth, bits +15-20%/yr against long-run price/bit declines). Every trailing CAGR is a trough-to-peak artefact and unusable as a forward proxy.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: All trailing CAGRs are measured from the FY23 trough (revenue $15.5bn, loss of $5.8bn) or the FY21 mid-cycle to the FY26 super-peak and diverge from each other and from any sustainable rate by far more than 30%. EPS and owner-FCF 3-yr CAGRs are undefined (negative FY23 base: EPS -5.34, owner FCF ~-6.7bn). FY16-FY26 10-yr revenue CAGR 26.8% and the FY18-peak-to-FY26-peak rate of 20.3%/yr are also cycle-inflated.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series (reported FCF less SBC incl. withholding less interest income): FY21 ~1.9bn, FY22 ~2.5bn, FY23 ~-6.7bn, FY24 ~-1.0bn, FY25 ~0.1bn, FY26 58.8bn. Cumulative FY15-FY25 reported FCF was only ~$15bn on ~$262bn of revenue (5.8%) - the through-cycle cash economics of memory before this cycle. The forward build assumes a structurally better mid-cycle than that history (SCA floors, HBM/data-centre mix, three-player DRAM oligopoly) but far below FY26-27.

scenario_narratives.base: Peak-and-normalise: FY27-28 at ~$245bn/86-82% margins (guidance-anchored), a 41% three-year revenue bust in FY29-31 as 2026-28 clean-room capex yields bits into an AI-capex digestion, then a structurally better mid-cycle (57-58% EBITDA margin vs a 42% FY14-25 average) because SCA floors cover ~35% of bits through 2030 and HBM/data-centre mix is permanent. Valued as a cyclical at 13x mid-cycle FCF.
scenario_narratives.bull: Durable supercycle: structurally constrained supply (HBM trade ratios, diminishing node returns, multi-year clean-room lead times) plus compounding agentic-AI demand keeps the market tight through 2030; SCAs extend and reset higher; revenue plateaus near $230-310bn at 66-68% margins.
scenario_narratives.bear: Classic memory bust from H2 FY27: inventory digestion, competitor bit growth, HBM4E share loss and floor renegotiations take revenue down 49% to FY30 with a 32% trough margin; the business reverts to its 42% historical mid-cycle margin at 26% capex intensity.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A memory maker is valued on its mid-cycle owner FCF plus the present value of the super-normal cash it banks before the cycle turns, never on the peak-year run-rate. FY26-27 are the peak: revenue is 6-8x cash cost against a 2.7x prior record, and the market values the company at a low single-digit multiple of FY27 earnings - which is the market itself saying a steep decline follows. The DCF therefore spends its effort on (i) how much cash arrives in FY27-28 (anchored to guidance, now net of a ~$54bn FY27 capex programme), (ii) how deep and how long the FY29-31 normalisation is, and (iii) what mid-cycle margin the SCAs, HBM mix and oligopoly structure make durable. House basis expenses SBC including the withholding paid on vested shares; interest income is stripped and the cash pile added once; the $12.9bn of repayable customer deposits and the $13.5bn of FY26 tax not yet paid are deducted from that pile as debt-like claims. Terminal value capped at 11-14x mid-cycle FCF, the range a buyer pays for a cyclical commodity producer.
key_risks_to_valuation: Cycle timing and depth: a one-year delay in the FY29 downturn adds ~$100bn of owner FCF (~$75/share after discounting); an earlier or deeper bust (bear) removes it. The base's -41% cumulative decline is a judgment, not a forecast.

Mid-cycle margin: each 5pp on the FY32-36 EBITDA margin is worth roughly $60-70/share through the terminal value. The 57-58% base rests on SCA floors that have never been tested in a down-market, and the 10-K's ~$134bn of remaining performance obligations at minimum pricing over five years (~$27-33bn a year) shows those floors sit well below current pricing.
Terminal multiple: 13x mid-cycle FCF vs 11x or 15x moves base value by ~+/-$55/share; the market today pays what is effectively a growth multiple on peak FCF.

Working-capital and tax unwind: FY26 OCF benefited from ~$13.5bn of income tax accrued but unpaid (now deducted in the bridge at face) and receivables ballooned; the receivables side is only approximated by the -12% WC capture.

Capex escalation: FY27 is now modelled at ~$54bn net from the 10-K guide (H1 ~$25bn, H2 'higher') with no full-year number given; every $5bn/yr above that is ~$4/share per year, and the extra supply it buys is the mechanism of the FY29-31 bust.
Geopolitics: US export controls and China's exclusion of Micron from critical infrastructure (CXMT/YMTC gaining) are priced through the share assumptions only indirectly.

Price volatility: the stock has ranged 192.59-1255.00 in 52 weeks and fell by more than a third in the seven weeks to this valuation in a sector-wide AI sell-off; the upside figures move daily while the drivers here change only on company evidence.

inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted ~1.15bn per FQ1-27 guidance, re-checked against the FY26 10-K: 1,131.4m basic shares outstanding at 2 Oct 2026 (cover page), FY26 weighted diluted 1,143m, Q4 FY26 weighted diluted 1,147m. Held FLAT: SBC incl. equity-award withholding is fully expensed in the flows, so diluting the count as well would charge it twice. Count funded by the $650m FY26 repurchase plus $1,127m of net-share-settlement withholding.
inputs.cash_note: Cash & equivalents 38,364 + short-term investments 5,070 + long-term marketable investments 30,019 at 3 Sep 2026 (FY26 10-K balance sheet, identical to the 30 Sept 8-K). Debt = current 491 + long-term 4,688. Two claims on this pile are deducted separately in equity_bridge: $12.9bn of customer deposits and $13.5bn of FY26 income tax accrued but not yet paid.
inputs.reported_fcf_basis: Company 'adjusted free cash flow' FY26: OCF 89,675 less investments in capital expenditures net of $3,316m government incentives (27,367). On gross capex (30,712) FCF is 58,963. Customer deposit proceeds (12,747) are classified in FINANCING by Micron, so OCF is not inflated by them.
inputs.sbc_source: FY26 cash flow statement add-back $1,333m (8-K EX-99.1, 2026-09-30) plus $1,127m 'repurchases of common stock - withholdings on employee equity awards' in financing. Micron publishes no combined figure, so the two lines are summed per the method. Withholding is large because vesting-date share value rose ~7x in the year.
inputs.interest_income_note: FY26 interest income $1,084m (Q4 run-rate $575m/qtr on the $73bn pile). Net cash ($68bn) exceeds the FCF base, so stripped from owner FCF; the cash is added back once in the bridge.
inputs.fiscal_year_end: 52/53-week year ending the Thursday nearest 31 August (FY26 ended 3 September 2026; EDGAR fye 0903)
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-11-18T21:00:01Z regular close (Yahoo Finance chart API); 52-week range 192.59-1255.00
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows discounted at a USD-built rate: 10-yr UST ~4.2% + 5.0% ERP x beta ~1.2-1.3 gives a cost of equity of 10.2-10.7%; debt is <0.5% of EV so WACC ~10.0%. Held at 10.0% in ALL THREE scenarios: memory-cycle risk is charged once, in the scenario flows and weights, not stacked into the discount rate (owner-fcf-adaptations section f).
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP ASC 842: operating-lease cost is expensed inside COGS/opex and therefore already charged within the EBITDA margin path; lease liabilities are immaterial (<1% of the cash pile) and are not added to debt. One treatment, applied once.
inputs.nci_treatment: None - no material non-controlling interest. Equity-method income ($59m FY26) is ignored.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (operating company), routed via dcf-methods SKILL.md row 2 (cyclical operating company) with owner-fcf-adaptations applied: risk charged once in the flows, single lease treatment, matching-asset rule (interest income stripped, cash added once). UPDATE of the 2026-10-02 build, not a rebuild - same model, same horizon, same scenario structure and weights; see reconciliation. WHAT CHANGED: (1) anchors refreshed to the FY2026 10-K (balance sheet and share count confirm the 8-K figures; no movement) and the 18 Nov close; (2) FY27 capex re-judged on the 10-K's first numeric guidance - net capex ~$11.5bn in FQ1, ~$25bn in H1, 'higher in the second half', i.e. ~$54bn against the ~$39bn modelled before - and FY28 capex lifted in base/bull because the H2-FY27 exit rate (>$27bn a half) is inconsistent with the earlier ~$42bn; (3) METHOD: the FY26 income tax accrued but unpaid ($13.5bn: provision ~14.76bn less 1.25bn cash paid; $9.82bn sits in noncurrent income taxes payable for Singapore Pillar Two top-up, the rest in current) moved from an approximate 2pp FY27 cash-tax uplift into the equity bridge as a debt-like claim, and the FY27 cash tax rate reset to the 16% run-rate so it is charged once. DELIBERATELY UNCHANGED: growth paths, EBITDA margin paths, SBC%, D&A% (the extra ~$21bn of FY27-28 capex adds ~2pp to FY29+ D&A/revenue, worth only a ~0.3pp-of-revenue tax shield, left out as a small conservatism), capex from FY29, WC capture, WACC, terminal growth and caps, and the 25/50/25 weights. The 36% share-price fall since 2 Oct is sector-wide (SOXX, NVDA and SK Hynix fell 28-37% over the same weeks) and Micron has disclosed nothing since the 30 Sept guidance; a price move alone is not evidence about the cycle. What would move them: the FQ1-27 print (late December) - contract pricing direction, bit shipments against the 'single-digit sequential' guide, any SCA renegotiation, FY27 capex total, and hyperscaler CY27 capex guides. CYCLE POSITION: FY26 is the steepest up-cycle in memory history (revenue 3.6x, GAAP gross margin 80.7%, Q4 run-rate $217bn/yr, FQ1-27 guided $61.5bn at ~86% GM). Revenue is running at ~6-8x the cash cost base against a FY18 peak of 2.7x and a FY14-25 average EBITDA margin of 42%, so NOTHING in the latest year is carried forward: every forecast year is built from components with the FY27 guidance year anchored to guidance and FY28+ set by judgment on where revenue/cost settles once clean rooms built now yield bits (late 2028+). 10-year horizon because margins only mature after the FY29-31 normalisation. CUSTOMER DEPOSITS: $12,895m noncurrent customer contract liabilities (take-or-pay Strategic Customer Agreements) are deducted in the bridge as debt-like - the 10-K confirms they are REPAYABLE, 'nearly all between 2029 and 2031', if customers meet minimum purchases; the cash is in the pile. Remaining performance obligations are ~$134bn at committed volumes and MINIMUM pricing, recognised within five years, about one quarter in the next twelve months: roughly $27-33bn a year of floor revenue, which says the floors sit far below today's pricing and protect less than '35% of bits' suggests. TAX: GAAP ETR 14.8% (Pillar Two 15% floor, Singapore); 16% cash rate throughout (Pillar Two floor plus a rising US share from the Idaho fabs). DATA: FY26 figures and the FY-end balance sheet are from the FY2026 10-K; Metrics.csv FY2026 row ties (revenue 133,188, OCF 89,675, gross capex 30,712).

bear.narrative: The cycle does what memory cycles have always done. Pricing rolls over in H2 FY27 as hyperscaler capex growth stalls and customers that bought ahead at 4-5x prices work down inventory; Samsung, SK Hynix and CXMT add bits aggressively into FY28-29; Micron loses HBM4E allocation to the two larger HBM suppliers; the 65% of uncontracted volume reprices down 60-70% (as in 2022-23) and some SCA counterparties push to renegotiate floors. Revenue falls 49% peak-to-trough (FY28 $229bn to FY30 $88bn), EBITDA margin troughs at 32% (above FY23's 13% because of the floors), and the business settles at its historical 42% mid-cycle margin with 26% capex intensity - the FY15-25 economics on a larger base. Owner FCF in the trough years is near zero; FY27-28 still deliver ~$185bn.
bear.capex_rationale: FY27 22.5% (~$51.5bn on ~$229bn): H1 is committed at ~$25bn and H2 is only trimmed once pricing rolls. FY28 unchanged at 20% (~$39bn) - a 25% cut in the bust, against 40% in FY23.

base.growth_rationale: FY27 +84% to ~$245bn: FQ1-27 guided $61.5bn with 'single-digit sequential bit growth', 75% of FY27 shipments already allocated/contracted, HBM pricing reset higher for CY27; held roughly flat across the year rather than compounding Q1. FY28 -6%: bits +12%, pricing begins to roll as the first new industry clean rooms and the CY27 HBM/CPU digestion arrive. FY29-31 -22/-20/-8 (cumulative -41%): the supply response built in FY26-28 (Micron construction capex alone rising for late-2028 clean rooms; Samsung/SK Hynix/CXMT likewise) meets a hyperscaler capex digestion; sits between the FY18-20 (-30%) and FY22-23 (-50%) busts, softened by SCA floors on ~35% of bits. FY32-36 +5-6%: bits +15-20%/yr against long-run price/bit declines, i.e. the memory industry's through-cycle revenue trend of 5-8%.
base.margin_rationale: FY27 86%: guided GM ~86%, opex ~$2.3bn/qtr (3.8%), D&A ~4.9% added back. FY28 82%: pricing softens faster than the cost base. FY29-31 74/64/58: revenue falls toward 2.3-2.5x cash cost. Mid-cycle 57-58%: ABOVE the FY14-25 average (42%) and the FY18 peak (65% in that year) because (i) SCA floor prices on ~35% of bits are stated to yield GM 'well above our peak quarterly margins in any past cycle' (>61%) through 2030, (ii) HBM/data-centre mix, (iii) three-player DRAM discipline; but BELOW anything the market is extrapolating from 87% today. D&A climbs from 7% to 17.5% of revenue as the $30-45bn/yr FY26-28 capex depreciates over a smaller revenue base; mid-cycle capex intensity settles at 22% (half the FY19-25 average of ~40%, because the structural revenue base is larger relative to equipment cost, and because D&A < capex is needed for 6% growth). Working capital: receivables + inventory far exceed payables (FY26: -$18.5bn on +$95.8bn revenue), so growth consumes ~12% of the revenue change and the FY29-31 decline releases it.
base.narrative: Peak-and-normalise. The AI build-out keeps memory sold out through FY28, Micron banks ~$240bn of owner FCF over FY27-28, then industry supply and a hyperscaler digestion bring a classic memory down-cycle in FY29-31 that bottoms well above any past trough because of SCA floors and HBM mix. The company that emerges is roughly FY26-sized in revenue by FY34 with 57-58% EBITDA margins, 22% capex intensity and ~27% owner-FCF margins - a far better business than the FY15-25 one, but a cyclical commodity producer capitalised at 13x mid-cycle FCF, not a software compounder.
base.capex_rationale: FY27 22.0% (~$54bn net of incentives on ~$245bn): 10-K guides ~$11.5bn FQ1, ~$25bn H1, 'higher in the second half'. FY28 21.0% (~$48bn): construction for late-2028 clean rooms continues at close to the H2-FY27 rate while the market is still sold out. FY29 onward unchanged (18.5-22%): spend is cut as revenue falls, as in FY23.

bull.narrative: Durable supercycle. Management's 'no line of sight to when supply and demand balances' proves right: HBM trade ratios (HBM4E) and diminishing node returns cap industry bit growth, agentic AI workloads and CPU-attached memory keep demand compounding, SCAs extend beyond 2030 at ceilings reset to today's pricing, and Micron holds its ~25% DRAM share into custom HBM4E with NVIDIA. Revenue peaks near $285bn in FY28, the FY29-31 air-pocket is only -22% cumulative, and the business plateaus as a 68%-EBITDA-margin oligopolist growing 7%/yr - memory re-rated from commodity to AI infrastructure.
bull.capex_rationale: FY27 21.0% (~$54.5bn on ~$260bn), FY28 20.0% (~$57bn): the same guided programme, extended as demand holds. FY29 onward unchanged at 18%.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 13x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Moved from the 15/50/35 house default to 25/50/25. Bear UP to 25%: memory has followed every up-cycle with a bust for forty years (FY12, FY16, FY19-20, FY23), FY26 margins are 2x any past peak, and a hyperscaler AI-capex digestion is a single macro event that would hit 60%+ of revenue at once. Bull DOWN to 25%: it requires several independent things to hold simultaneously - AI capex compounding through 2030, no effective supply response from Samsung/SK Hynix/CXMT despite record industry capex, SCA ceilings/floors surviving a soft market, and Micron keeping HBM share into custom HBM4E. Symmetric weights around a base that already sits far above the company's own through-cycle history.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
